title: Geometry - Lesson 4 Practice: Triangle Similarity SSS and SAS
description: Practice choosing SSS Similarity, SAS Similarity, or not enough evidence from proportional side information.

questions.question: Two triangles have corresponding side lengths 4, 6, 8 and 10, 15, 20. Which theorem proves the triangles are similar?
questions.explanation: All three corresponding side ratios match: 4/10 = 6/15 = 8/20 = 2/5. That is SSS Similarity.

questions.question: Two triangles have side pairs 6 and 9, 8 and 12, and the included angles between those sides are congruent. Which theorem proves similarity?
options: No theorem applies because only two side pairs are given
questions.explanation: The side ratios match, 6/9 = 8/12 = 2/3, and the congruent angle is included between those sides. That is SAS Similarity.

questions.question: SSS Similarity requires all three pairs of corresponding sides to be proportional.
questions.explanation: SSS Similarity is based on three matching side ratios.

questions.question: Which set of side lengths can prove two triangles are similar by SSS Similarity?
questions.explanation: The ratios 4/8, 6/12, and 9/18 all equal 1/2, so the triangles are similar by SSS Similarity.

questions.question: For SAS Similarity, where must the congruent angle be located?
questions.explanation: SAS uses two proportional side pairs and the included angle, which is the angle between those two sides.

questions.question: Two triangles have corresponding side ratios 5/15, 7/21, and 9/27. These ratios all simplify to ______.
questions.explanation: Each ratio simplifies to 1/3, so the side evidence would support SSS Similarity.

questions.question: Two triangles have side pairs 5 and 10, 8 and 16, and a congruent angle that is not between those two sides. Which conclusion is best?
options: The triangles are similar by SAS Similarity.
The triangles are similar by SSS Similarity.
The evidence is not enough for SSS or SAS Similarity.
The triangles are congruent by SAS.
questions.explanation: SAS Similarity requires the congruent angle to be included between the proportional sides. SSS also cannot be used because only two side pairs are given.

questions.question: Explain how to decide between SSS Similarity and SAS Similarity when reading triangle evidence.
questions.correctAnswer: Use SSS Similarity when all three corresponding side pairs are proportional. Use SAS Similarity when two corresponding side pairs are proportional and the included angles are congruent.
questions.explanation: The theorem depends on the evidence: three side ratios for SSS, or two side ratios plus the included angle for SAS.
